image_description: A sturgeon swimming in an aquarium environment with a gravel substrate and dark background. The fish is positioned horizontally, showing its dorsal side and left flank. There are significant white, ghost-like artifacts overlaying the head and anterior body of the fish, resembling melted plastic or double-exposure errors.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Occluded by the same white artifacts affecting the head; barbels are not visible.
The snout area is distorted and covered by artifacting, preventing verification of shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The main torso of the fish is visible and exhibits the correct elongated, cylindrical shape typical of a sturgeon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct ridges and bony plates (scutes) are visible along the lateral line and dorsal ridge, matching sturgeon anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin shows dark gray/black coloration on top, consistent with the class description.
The caudal fin is visible at the rear and displays the characteristic asymmetrical lobes of a heterocercal tail.
